objective: Determine whether adding more direct secure-DNS upstreams improves censorship resilience without introducing resolver leakage, latency or unproven failover.

methodEvidence.source: Control D official free DNS documentation
methodEvidence.claim: Control D free resolvers support encrypted DNS and use 76.76.2.11 / 76.76.10.11 as Secure DNS bootstrap IPs.
Policy upstream lists provide ordered fallback on timeout; leak_on_upstream_failure=false prevents OS-resolver fallback.

cloudflare.directUrlProbe: https://1.1.1.1/dns-query returned HTTP 400 with valid TLS, proving basic HTTPS reachability

orderedFailoverSimulation.ctrldObserved: attempted upstream.0 then upstream.1 as designed
orderedFailoverSimulation.outcome: both failed on current network; no useful fallback

decision.rationale: Only the current direct-IP Control D endpoint produced real DNS answers. Adding unavailable upstreams would add latency/failure surface without improving outcome. OS-resolver leakage remains disabled.
decision.future: Re-evaluate on another network or if an independently proven direct secure-DNS endpoint passes actual DNS-message round trips.
